Room temperature is not numerically specified. The selenium stock self-heats to about 80 °C; cooling or equilibration before the reported room-temperature precipitation is not described. No external heating step is inferred.
Precipitation is described as rapid and occurring at once; numerical mixing/aging duration, stirring rate, vessel type/capacity and recovered yield are unreported.
Acid/water wash volumes and repetition count, filtration hardware and vacuum pressure are unreported.
EDTA is named without salt/counterion or starting protonation state. The alcohol for optical-sample dispersion is unnamed; neither ethanol nor methanol is inferred.
The statement that all reagents were 99.9% purity does not specify individual water/solution assays. Distilled water is explicitly named.

source_notes.label: Alkaline selenium source
source_notes.summary: The authors propose selenide, selenite and polyselenide species in the deep-red stock and report stability only with OH− concentration greater than 10 M. The value describes the source explanation, not a separately measured batch concentration.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, Equations 1–2 and selenium-source discussion

source_notes.label: Cadmium complex
source_notes.summary: The authors attribute reduced hydroxide by-product to cadmium complexation and discuss release of Cd2+ as precipitation proceeds. The source reports no CdSeO3 detected by XRD or XPS. No separate quantified bare-cadmium control recipe or measured by-product fraction is supplied.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Equations 3–5 and mechanism discussion

source_notes.label: Workup and excess reagents
source_notes.summary: The source says dilute 0.1 M HCl can remove small Cd(OH)2 amounts and water can remove excess cadmium complex; excess elemental Se can precipitate during washing and be difficult to remove. These are conditional source explanations, not extra measured batches.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 3, Workup and stoichiometry discussion

source_notes.label: Temperature scope
source_notes.summary: About 80 °C is the self-heating selenium-stock temperature. The source separately describes CdSe precipitation at room temperature; no stock-cooling interval is given.
